html:
SMTO-FIL-0025 — A file changed while SMTO was working with it

GUID: bca938a3-745e-49e1-9022-638f2d2c2b88
Slug: file-revision-conflict
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The file or folder was changed, replaced or moved by someone or something else after SMTO last looked at it, or while it was working. SMTO stopped instead of overwriting those changes.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close or pause other programs, people or sync tools (such as cloud-drive syncing) that may be changing the same files. SMTO stops whenever the file changes underneath it, so the file must hold still.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to look at the file again and redo the change based on what is there now. Its earlier view of the file is out of date, and a fresh look keeps the other changes.
  3. If SMTO was copying, moving or deleting several items, check both locations to see what already happened before asking it to continue. Some items may have been handled before the change was noticed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the step and the file keeps both the other changes and SMTO's change.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to force its version over the file before you've checked what changed; that could erase the other changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation detected that the target's identity changed: the current stat revision, parent directory, symlink target or preserved extended attributes no longer match the expected revision or the state observed before or during the operation.

What this means

  • Current file, parent, revision, content hash, symlink target or preserved metadata differs from the identity expected before or during the operation. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Current file, parent, revision, content hash, symlink target or preserved metadata differs from the identity expected before or during the operation.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare expected/current revisions and per-item completion facts; do not assume earlier steps were undone.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the path's current content and revision, review the concurrent change, and resubmit with the fresh expected_revision; check changed_paths and partial_mutation in the receipt for multi-entry copy, move or delete work already done. Do not disable revision checks (gateway_core/file_common.regular/unchanged/expected, file_manage, transfer_paths.check_parent, skills/gateway/copy.py).
  • Read the current content and revision, then reapply the intended edit against that revision. Never blindly overwrite.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh reads establish current state and any intended new edit uses that reviewed revision.

What not to do

  • Do not reuse the stale revision or disable revision checking.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-MEM-0006 — This memory changed before your change was saved
  • SMTO-KV-0006 — A scratch note changed before the Agent could update it
